verdict.rationale: Unreal Engine provides official, first-party programming interfaces to build against. Its documented C++ gameplay programming API includes the reflection system and delegates. Its Python editor-scripting API has a generated per-class reference and official autocomplete stub generation. Its Remote Control HTTP/WebSocket API can call any Blueprint-callable function. missing for 10: the Python API is marked Experimental, there are no packaged client SDK libraries for the Remote Control API, and there is no independent or hands-on corroboration of building against these SDKs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Creating new Gameplay classes in C++, and all changes will be reflected in the Unreal Editor after compiling with either Visual Studio or XCode.
Python API sections: Modules, Native Types, Struct Types, Class Types, Enum Types
Before setting up autocomplete, you will need to tell the Unreal Engine (UE) Python Plugin to generate the necessary stubs.

You can call any function that is callable from Blueprint. This includes any function defined in C++ with the BlueprintCallable specifier, or any function that is defined and implemented entirely in Blueprint.
Plugins can add runtime gameplay functionality, modify built-in Engine features (or add new ones), create new file types, and extend the capabilities of the Editor
